title: Thirteen colonies
hook: An Atlantic strip becomes an independent union.
notes: Original Orbis factual synthesis; linked federal records and historic-site accounts, checked 14 October 2026. Points locate places approximately, not territorial extents. Modern national/state outlines are reference geography, never reconstructed historical borders. No archival images or source prose redistributed. Sources by scene: Jamestown: a river foothold: https://www.nps.gov/jame/learn/historyculture/a-short-history-of-jamestown.htm; Plymouth: an inhabited shore: https://www.nps.gov/rowi/learn/historyculture/wampanoag.htm; A declaration in Philadelphia: https://www.archives.gov/founding-docs/declaration; Thirteen names, an international treaty: https://www.archives.gov/milestone-documents/treaty-of-paris Supplementary date/location evidence: https://www.nps.gov/jame/faqs.htm.

scenes.title: Jamestown: a river foothold
scenes.text: English settlers established Jamestown in 1607 on the James River, within Powhatan country. Its coastal location connected the settlement to Atlantic shipping.

scenes.title: Plymouth: an inhabited shore
scenes.text: The land that became Plymouth Colony was Wampanoag land. The point locates Plymouth rather than outlining either Indigenous territory or a colonial claim.

scenes.title: A declaration in Philadelphia
scenes.text: In 1776 the Declaration of Independence announced separation from Britain. Philadelphia is the location of the congressional decision, not a frontier between armies.

scenes.title: Thirteen names, an international treaty
scenes.text: The Treaty of Paris of 1783 named the thirteen states and recognised US independence. British recognition was a diplomatic act; it did not obtain Indigenous consent to the treaty’s western claims. The coloured shapes locate their modern successor states; colonial claims extended beyond these outlines.
